chunks: ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā al-Sābāṭī asked Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about a man who finds a mouse in his vessel, after having performed wudu (ablution) from that vessel several times, washed his clothes from it, and performed ghusl from it, while the mouse had been decomposed.

So he said: “If he had seen it in the vessel before performing ghusl, or wudu (ablution), or washing his clothes, and then did that after seeing it in the vessel, then he must wash his clothes, wash everything that that water touched, and repeat the wudu (ablution) and the salat (prayer). But if he only saw it after he had finished all that and done it, then he should not touch any of the water, and there is nothing upon him, because he does not know when it fell into it.”
Then he said: “Perhaps it only fell into it at that very hour in which he saw it.”

key_terms.إِنَائِهِ: his vessel or container holding the water
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: salat (prayer), which must be repeated in the specified case
key_terms.الْمَاءِ: the water whose purity status is under discussion
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual washing before salat (prayer)
key_terms.سَقَطَتْ: fell into, referring to the mouse entering the water
key_terms.فَأْرَةً: a mouse, the source of impurity in this case

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone finds a dead mouse in water after using it for wudu (ablution), ghusl, or washing clothes?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about water contaminated by a dead mouse and the effect of prior knowledge on ritual acts. If the impurity was known before using the water, the affected acts and items must be redone or washed; if discovered only afterward, no liability is established because the time of contamination is unknown.
